name: heralded_memory_memory
label_authority: Elicit run of 18 Oct 2026 as saved. Five benchmarks are the answer's own; the rest are its included set. DOIs come from the tool export, which also resolves the two DOIs QUESTION.md had noted as written from memory. No human verification.
identity_rule: DOI or verified work identity; title-only matches require adjudication
question: Which experiments have demonstrated heralded entanglement between two remote quantum memories, and what herald rate, Bell-state fidelity and storage time of the entangled state did each report?
reference: Elicit answer, 18 Oct 2026, saved in notes/test-questions/heralded-memory-memory/ with its papers export. The question wording was reconstructed from the answer. Overlaps stored_qubit_entanglement but asks for the measured lifetime of the remote entangled pair, not local memory coherence.
expected_direction: Five benchmarks with rate, fidelity and entangled-state storage kept apart: Stephenson 182/s at 94.0 ± 0.5% with no storage figure; Humphreys 6/s at 81 ± 2% or 39/s at 60 ± 2% with 200 ± 10 ms remote coherence; van Leent one herald per 85 s over 33 km at >= 62.2 ± 1.5%, read at 171-178 microseconds; Knaut 69 ± 7% over 35 km with 500 ms, 1 s with error detection; Hanni 510 heralds/s, 0.32 readouts/s, 81 ± 1% effective fidelity, up to 25 microseconds. Caveats: local memory coherence is not the lifetime of the remote pair, and a vacuum-excluded effective fidelity is not an unconditional Bell fidelity.

answer_elements.question: Storage time of the entangled state, with "not reported" where the paper gives none

Comparability caveats: local memory coherence is not the entangled-pair lifetime, vacuum-excluded effective fidelity is not an unconditional Bell fidelity, and Knaut's 1 pair/s rate is not paired with the 35 km / 1 s operating point

pass_rule.status: draft from QUESTION.md, not confirmed by the owner
rules: At least 4 of the 5 benchmark papers are found, and Humphreys 2017 reaches the answer with its 200 ms entangled-state coherence taken from a located passage.

The answer keeps the caveats: local memory coherence is not the lifetime of the entangled pair; vacuum-excluded effective fidelity is not an unconditional Bell fidelity; Knaut's 1 /s rate is not paired with the 35 km / 1 s operating point.
The answer says "not reported" when a number is missing; it never fills the gap from another experiment.
